title: Design an Elevator System
summary: A box that goes up and down is a scheduling problem wearing a disguise. The class diagram takes ten minutes; the hour is decided by which car answers a hall call, and whether you can defend the answer.

refs.note: Worked breakdown with the requirement framing and the dispatch discussion.

refs.title: Elevator System Low-Level Design
refs.note: Requirements, class breakdown and a reference implementation.

blocks.title: What you are actually being asked
blocks.text: Everyone can draw `Elevator`, `Floor`, `Button`. Nobody gets hired for that. The question is **which car answers a hall call, and why** — and whether you understand that a hall call and a car call are different things. Get the classes down fast and spend the time on dispatch.

A building with *F* floors and *C* elevator cars. People press an up or down button on a floor; people inside a car press a destination floor. Move the cars so everyone gets where they are going without anyone waiting forever.

blocks.title: Hall call versus car call
blocks.text: A **hall call** is *“someone on floor 7 wants to go down”* — it has a direction and no destination, and any car can serve it. A **car call** is *“the person in car 2 wants floor 3”* — it has a destination, no direction, and only that car can serve it. Conflating the two is the single most common modelling error, and it makes correct dispatch impossible.

items.title: How many cars, how many floors?
items.text: One car is a toy. The whole problem is dispatch across several, so confirm C > 1 or you are answering a different question.

items.title: Are there express cars, or floor restrictions?
items.text: Basements, penthouses and service cars turn dispatch into a constrained search. Confirm scope before you build for it.

items.title: What is being optimised — wait time or travel time?
items.text: They are different objectives and they disagree. Average wait, worst-case wait, and total energy give three different schedulers. Pick one out loud.

items.title: Capacity limits?
items.text: If a car can be full, dispatch has to model load and a full car has to skip a hall call it already accepted.

items.title: Real time, or simulated ticks?
items.text: Say you will model time as discrete steps. It makes the design testable and sidesteps a thread-per-elevator discussion you do not need yet.

blocks.title: Cars own movement, the controller owns policy
blocks.caption: `ElevatorCar` knows how to move and nothing about fairness. `Dispatcher` knows about fairness and nothing about motors. That seam is what the follow-ups will push on.
blocks.code:
classDiagram
    class ElevatorSystem {
        -List~ElevatorCar~ cars
        -Dispatcher dispatcher
        +void hallCall(int floor, Direction d)
        +void carCall(int carId, int floor)
        +void step()
    }
    class ElevatorCar {
        -int id
        -int currentFloor
        -Direction direction
        -DoorState doors
        -TreeSet~Integer~ stopsAhead
        +void addStop(int floor)
        +void step()
        +boolean canServe(int floor, Direction d)
    }
    class Dispatcher {
        <<interface>>
        +ElevatorCar select(List~ElevatorCar~ cars, HallCall call)
    }
    class HallCall {
        -int floor
        -Direction direction
    }
    ElevatorSystem o-- ElevatorCar
    ElevatorSystem --> Dispatcher
    Dispatcher ..> HallCall
    Dispatcher <|.. NearestCarDispatcher
    Dispatcher <|.. LookDispatcher

blocks.text: The car is a state machine

blocks.title: One car, four states
blocks.caption: Doors are a state, not a boolean. A car with open doors cannot move, and every real-world safety rule hangs off that fact.
blocks.code:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> MovingUp : stop above
    Idle --> MovingDown : stop below
    MovingUp --> DoorsOpen : arrived at a stop
    MovingDown --> DoorsOpen : arrived at a stop
    MovingUp --> MovingUp : more stops above
    MovingDown --> MovingDown : more stops below
    DoorsOpen --> Idle : no stops left
    DoorsOpen --> MovingUp : stops above
    DoorsOpen --> MovingDown : stops below

blocks.text: Dispatch — where the interview is won
Three answers, in ascending order of how impressed the interviewer will be.

blocks.caption: The third one is what real controllers do.
rows: First free car, in request order
A car passes your floor going the right way and does not stop. Obviously wrong to anyone who has used a lift
Ignores direction: sends a car that is moving away, and starves the top floors
Prefer a car already moving toward the call **in the same direction**; otherwise the nearest idle car
This is the real answer. Cost is bounded worst-case wait, which is the trade you name

blocks.title: The sentence that lands
blocks.text: *“I would use a LOOK sweep: a car keeps going one direction, serves everything ahead of it, and only reverses when nothing is left that way. Fairness comes out of the sweep for free, instead of me maintaining a fairness counter.”*

blocks.title: A set, not a list
blocks.text: Pressing 5 twice must not queue two stops. Using a `Set` makes that true by construction instead of by an `if (!stops.contains(f))` you will forget somewhere.

blocks.caption: `C` cars, `F` floors, `S` stops queued on one car.
rows: O(C × F) worst case, one stop per floor per car

blocks.text: Buttons are pressed by people, so calls arrive from many threads while the simulation loop is moving cars.

items: **Each car owns its own stop set.** Give every car a lock, or a single-threaded actor loop fed by a queue. Do not put one lock around the whole building.

**Dispatch reads car state while cars mutate it.** The scores are a snapshot and will be slightly stale — that is acceptable for a scheduling hint and you should say so rather than locking every car to score it.
**Assignment must be atomic.** Two hall calls dispatched concurrently can both pick the same idle car and both assume it is theirs. Assign under the car's own lock, and re-check it is still idle.

items.title: Add capacity and weight limits
items.text: The car reports load; a full car stops accepting hall calls but must still serve car calls from the people inside. Dispatch has to skip it *without* dropping the call.

items.title: Add express cars and floor restrictions
items.text: `canServe(floor)` per car, checked before scoring. It turns dispatch into a filter-then-score, which is a one-line change if the interface is right.

items.title: Emergency and maintenance mode
items.text: A state on the car that drops every stop and returns to a designated floor. Worth mentioning that safety overrides are never a strategy — they bypass the dispatcher entirely.

items.title: Optimise for energy rather than wait
items.text: Swap the dispatcher. If the interviewer asks and your answer is “swap the dispatcher”, the design worked.

items.title: Prove nobody starves
items.text: LOOK bounds worst-case wait at roughly two full sweeps. Nearest-car does not, and that is the concrete reason to prefer it.

items.title: A building with 100 floors and 20 cars
items.text: Zoning: cars serve floor bands so sweeps are shorter. This is the HLD pivot — the same reasoning as sharding.

blocks.text: Edge cases to state before you are asked

items: Same floor pressed twice → one stop, because stops are a set.
A hall call on the floor a car is already stopped at with doors open → serve it now, do not queue it.
All cars busy → the call queues; it must not be dropped or reassigned twice.
Requesting the floor you are already on → doors open, no movement.
A car reversing with stops both above and below → LOOK finishes the current direction first; verify it does not oscillate.

rows: Separates hall calls from car calls
A sorted set — dedupe and directional lookup for free
A `Dispatcher` interface, swapped in the follow-up
Per-car locking, and dispatch scores as a stale snapshot

blocks.title: The 45-minute plan
blocks.text: **0–6** clarify cars, floors, objective. **6–10** hall call versus car call — get this on the board early. **10–18** classes and the car state machine. **18–30** code the car's `step` and one dispatcher. **30–38** compare FCFS, nearest and LOOK out loud. **38–45** capacity or zoning.
